minutes.headline: Zoning Board granted Hannaford a special permit alteration for outdoor plant, flower and produce displays, with size limits.
minutes.summary: The board heard Hannaford's application to display seasonal plants outside its store at 333 Mass Ave. A resident opposed it on fire lane, safety and theft grounds. The board added conditions on area, location and type of goods, and the chair announced the permit granted. The applicant must still go to the Planning Board for site plan review.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted Hannaford an alteration to its special permit for outdoor displays of seasonal plants, flowers and produce at 333 Mass Ave.
The grant limits the display to a set area on each side of the store, with conditions on location and type of goods; the vote tally was not audible.
A resident opposed the request, citing the 1993 permit's indoor-sales assumption, past displays in fire lanes, and theft and policing concerns.
The resident said she took photos showing displays in the fire lane despite enforcement attempts, and that the product could be sold inside.
The chair told the applicant the next step is site plan review with the Planning Board.

why_it_matters: This changes what a neighborhood grocery store may put outside on town-regulated land, and it touches fire lane access and safety at a busy Mass Ave site.
watch_next: Hannaford's site plan review before the Planning Board, which the chair named as the next step; no date was given in the minutes.
